title: Beth Din misconduct evidence-state baseline — issue #2646
summary: Bounded first pass separating an adjudicated federal get-coercion case from two distinct 2026 New York civil-review records that do not establish misconduct on the merits.

caveats: The pass is intentionally bounded and does not claim issue #2646 is complete.
The 2013 federal case involved a specific ad-hoc beth din convened in Martin Wolmark's office; no connection to Beth Din of America is asserted.
The Redacted v Redacted misconduct allegation was not adjudicated because the proceedings settled and were discontinued.
Mittel was dismissed on arbitral-immunity grounds; that disposition does not adjudicate the merits of misconduct allegations.

data.research_question: What can be established from primary public records about Beth Din misconduct/coercion without conflating distinct tribunals or promoting allegations into findings?
data.method: Bounded primary-source pass using U.S. Department of Justice records, official New York court opinions, and Beth Din of America first-party rules; packet kept under digs/ for canonical import/merge validation.

findings.finding: PROVEN/ADJUDICATED: Martin Wolmark pleaded guilty to conspiracy to travel in interstate commerce to commit extortion and received a 38-month sentence. Official records state that Wolmark, Mendel Epstein, and Jay Goldstein convened an ad-hoc beth din in Wolmark's office on October 2, 2013 as part of the planned forced-get operation.

PROVEN/ADJUDICATED: Mendel Epstein was convicted at trial of conspiracy to commit kidnapping and sentenced to 120 months; Binyamin Stimler was convicted of conspiracy and attempted kidnapping and sentenced to 39 months. These convictions corroborate the criminal coercion scheme but do not identify the ad-hoc beth din as Beth Din of America.

ALLEGED / NOT ADJUDICATED: Matter of Redacted v Redacted records a challenge to a Beth Din of America award alleging irrationality and refusal to hear evidence. The proceedings settled and were discontinued in October 2025.

PROCEDURAL / NOT A MISCONDUCT MERITS FINDING: Mittel v The Beth Din of the United States of America, Inc. affirmed dismissal because agreed rules conferred arbitral immunity. The exact captioned organization remains separate pending identity evidence.
INSTITUTIONAL BASELINE: Beth Din of America publishes arbitration rules/procedures; those rules support later governance comparison but are not proof of compliance or violation in a particular case.
